body.t: On 21 December 2026 London's civil dawn is about 07:23 and dusk about 16:33 (computed) — the whole usable day, twilight included, fits inside a working day, with true daylight just 7 hours 50 minutes of it.

New York's midsummer civil twilight lasts about 33 minutes each end (sunrise 05:24, civil dawn 04:51). Toward the equator it shrinks toward 20 minutes; toward the poles it can stretch for hours — the Sun's slant is everything.

faq: At −6° the sky's brightness drops to roughly the level where artificial light takes over for ordinary outdoor activity — the convention almanacs, aviation and many laws adopted. Like all twilight bounds it is a chosen standard on a smooth dimming curve.
Is civil dawn the same as first light?

In everyday speech, near enough. Formally this page computes the −6° crossing; 'first light' in military and hunting usage usually means the start of civil twilight — the same instant wearing a field name.
How long does civil twilight last where I live?

Roughly 20–25 minutes near the equator, about half an hour at mid-latitudes, and hours near the poles in season. Latitude and date set it — the calculator answers for your point rather than the average.
Can civil twilight last all night?

Yes — poleward of about 60.5° latitude at the solstice the Sun never reaches −6°, and 'night' is one long civil twilight. White nights in St Petersburg and Reykjavik are this geometry with better poetry.
Does weather change the computed times?
The times are astronomical and fixed; clouds decide whether the light feels like the definition. A stormy dusk goes dark early in practice while the computed boundary stands.
Aviation leans on civil twilight too (night definitions in many regulations reference it), while mariners own the nautical grade and astronomers the 18° line. One staircase, three professions.
Civil dusk is the evening crossing, civil dawn the morning one. The pair bound the night; each day's twilight length is the same geometry read in two directions, weather permitting.
